clauses.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11206 Providing for inspection of interest equalization tax returns" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.
clauses.reason: whole: The order directs that returns made in respect of the tax imposed by chapter 41 of the Internal Revenue Code shall be open to inspection by certain classes of persons and government establishments under the Treasury rules it names, and says it is effective on filing for publication. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11206 Providing for inspection of interest equalization tax returns"). The order has no end date of its own. research_rationale:
EO 11206 (1965-03-18, 30 FR 3741) is an order under section 6103(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, as amended by section 3(c) of the Interest Equalization Tax Act, opening certain interest equalization tax returns to inspection. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11206.txt, 30 FR 3741, PDF pages 7-7) and confirmed its number, title and signature date against the census register. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes it by number; the dossier already carries the agent-located, independently upheld ACT record for that revocation, which I checked against the held EO 12553 text (operative sentence and table row "11206 Providing for inspection of interest equalization tax returns"). The first end is that express revocation. savings.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text), so nothing of this order continues after the revocation. Inspections that were lawfully made while the order was in force are completed acts accrued before the revocation; the Treasury regulations the order refers to are separate instruments that the held sources do not tie to the order's continued operation.
